guarantees.claim: lfsr_en is the logical OR of ctrl_lfsr_en, data_lfsr_en, and sideload_lfsr_en.
ctrl_rand[0] is continuously assigned the upper 32 bits of the LFSR state (lfsr[63:32]).
ctrl_rand[1] is continuously assigned the result of perm_data(lfsr[31:0], RndCnstRandPerm).
data_rand[1] is continuously assigned the result of perm_data(lfsr[63:32], RndCnstRandPerm).
The prim_lfsr instance's entropy_i input is tied to all zeros.
The LFSR enable input lfsr_en_i is driven by the signal lfsr_en (the OR of the three domain enables).
The LFSR seed enable and seed data are directly connected to the outputs of the keymgr_reseed_ctrl instance.
The LFSR state output is connected to the lfsr signal, which drives the random generation assignments.
The design enforces at elaboration that LfsrWidth equals 64 via an ASSERT_INIT.
The reseed_interval_i input of u_reseed_ctrl is connected to the register field reg2hw.reseed_interval_shadowed.q.

assumptions.claim: The signals ctrl_lfsr_en, data_lfsr_en, and sideload_lfsr_en (not assigned in this chunk) are driven to 1 only when the LFSR should advance and to 0 otherwise to prevent unnecessary toggling or stalling.
assumptions.risk: If all enables are low during a required reseed, the LFSR stalls and randomness becomes stale. If any enable is high when no operation is active, the LFSR toggles, potentially leaking state via power side-channel.

formal_sketch.consequent: The signals ctrl_lfsr_en, data_lfsr_en, and sideload_lfsr_en (not assigned in this chunk) are driven to 1 only when the LFSR should advance and to 0 otherwise to prevent unnecessary toggling or stalling

assumptions.claim: The seed value driven by keymgr_reseed_ctrl on seed_o when seed_en is asserted must have sufficient entropy and not be predictable or constant.
assumptions.risk: If the seed is weak or known, the LFSR output sequence becomes deterministic, breaking the randomness used for masking and potentially enabling key recovery via side-channel analysis.

formal_sketch.consequent: The seed value driven by keymgr_reseed_ctrl on seed_o when seed_en is asserted must have sufficient entropy and not be predictable or constant

assumptions.claim: The external EDN module connected to edn_o/edn_i must provide entropy upon reseed requests; if it fails, reseeding may not complete.
assumptions.cond: when reseed_req is asserted and reseed controller initiates EDN request
assumptions.risk: Without EDN response, the LFSR seed is never updated, leading to stale randomness and potential predictability of masked values.

formal_sketch.antecedent: when reseed_req is asserted and reseed controller initiates EDN request
formal_sketch.consequent: The external EDN module connected to edn_o/edn_i must provide entropy upon reseed requests; if it fails, reseeding may not complete

assumptions.claim: The register field reg2hw.reseed_interval_shadowed.q must contain a valid, non-zero reseed interval value; otherwise the reseed controller may fail or reseed too frequently.
assumptions.risk: An invalid interval could cause either no reseeding (stale randomness) or excessive reseeding (denial of service, power side-channel amplification).

formal_sketch.consequent: The register field reg2hw.reseed_interval_shadowed.q must contain a valid, non-zero reseed interval value; otherwise the reseed controller may fail or reseed too frequently

uncertain_points.claim: The LFSR entropy_i input is tied to zero; the entire randomness source is the deterministic LFSR seeded only by the reseed controller. If the seed is ever predictable or captured, all subsequent ctrl_rand/data_rand values become predictable. Is continuous entropy mixing required?
uncertain_points.risk: An attacker who knows the seed can compute future random shares, breaking the side-channel resistance of masked operations and potentially recovering secret keys.

formal_sketch.consequent: The LFSR entropy_i input is tied to zero; the entire randomness source is the deterministic LFSR seeded only by the reseed controller. If the seed is ever predictable or captured, all subsequent ctrl_rand/data_rand values become predictable

uncertain_points.claim: The assignments ctrl_rand[0] = lfsr[63:32] and data_rand[0] = lfsr[31:0] assume RandWidth ≤ 32, else the upper bits of the share vectors are zero-filled (or if RandWidth > 32 the LHS width mismatch zero-extends). Conversely, if RandWidth < 32, bits are truncated. This could create non-uniform or biased randomness.
uncertain_points.risk: Non-uniform share distribution may weaken the masking effect, potentially allowing an attacker to correlate power traces with secret keys.

formal.consequent: ctrl_rand[0][31:0] == lfsr[63:32] (and zero/truncation on upper/lower bits)

security_implications: ctrl_rand and data_rand are used for masked key operations; if LFSR-based randomness is predictable due to fixed seed, zero entropy, or parameter width mismatches, an attacker could perform side-channel attacks to recover secret keys. The reseed_cnt_err output may indicate a failure in reseeding; if unhandled, the LFSR could remain stale, further compromising masking effectiveness.
